draft.title: The transmission mechanism
card: The transmission mechanism is how a change in the cash rate reaches spending in the economy. It works through four channels.
Saving and investment
when rates rise, saving pays more and borrowing costs more, so households and firms tend to spend and invest less. Falling rates tend to do the reverse.
Cash flow
many borrowers have variable rate loans. A rate rise lifts their repayments and leaves less income to spend. A rate fall frees up income.
Exchange rate

higher Australian rates can attract foreign funds and lift the dollar, which makes exports dearer and imports cheaper. Lower rates tend to do the opposite. Asset prices and wealth is the fourth channel: rates also tend to move prices of houses and shares in the opposite direction, which changes how wealthy owners feel.
draft.remember: A rate change reaches spending through four channels, and each one works by changing what people and firms can or will spend.

a.q: The RBA raises the cash rate, and banks lift variable home loan rates. Households pay more each month and have less left to spend. Which channel is this?
opts: Cash flow
Saving and investment
The exchange rate
Asset prices and wealth
a.why: The higher repayments cut the income households have left to spend, which is the cash flow channel. Saving and investment is about the reward for saving and the cost of new borrowing, not the squeeze on repayments of existing loans.
a.clue: Think about what is left of income after the loan repayment.

b.q: The RBA cuts the cash rate. Foreign investors move funds out of Australia, and the dollar falls. What is the likely effect through the exchange rate channel?
opts: Exports get cheaper abroad, so demand tends to rise
Exports get dearer abroad, so demand tends to rise
Exports get cheaper abroad, so demand tends to fall
Imports get cheaper, so demand for local goods tends to rise
b.why: A lower dollar makes Australian goods cheaper for overseas buyers, so export demand tends to rise. This adds to the effect of the rate cut. Imports become dearer, not cheaper, when the dollar falls.
b.clue: A weaker dollar buys less foreign money for each Australian dollar.

b.best: Exports get cheaper abroad, so demand tends to rise

problems.detail: The fourth channel (asset prices and wealth) is tucked into the end of the exchange rate bullet instead of having its own bullet. Students may read it as part of the exchange rate channel, or miss that it is a separate fourth channel.

check.summary: Facts and both questions are sound, and the intended answers are the only right options. The card puts the asset prices and wealth channel inside the exchange rate bullet; it should be its own bullet.

proposal.title: The transmission mechanism
card: Saving and investment
higher rates reward saving and raise the cost of new borrowing, so households and firms tend to spend and invest less. Lower rates tend to do the reverse.

many borrowers have variable rate loans, so a rate rise lifts their repayments and leaves less income to spend. A rate cut frees up income.
Exchange rate
higher Australian rates can attract foreign funds and lift the dollar, making exports dearer and imports cheaper. Lower rates can lower the dollar, making exports cheaper and imports dearer.
Asset prices and wealth
lower rates tend to lift house and share prices, and higher rates tend to lower them. Owners who feel wealthier tend to spend more.
